completion.text: {"adjudications":[{"id":"F1","decision":"confirmed","reason":"The revision deleted the Delane sentence. 'He had never heard of young Adams' now follows a sentence whose subject is Adams, so the pronoun points to the wrong man. Delane's ignorance of his victim is the irony of the scene.","evidence":[{"document":"013.revision","paragraph":5,"quote":"He was thinking of Delane, whose eye caught his at the moment of Milnes's embrace. He had never heard of young Adams"},{"document":"013.source","paragraph":5,"quote":"Delane probably regarded it as a piece of Milnes's foolery; he had never heard of young Adams"}]},{"id":"F2","decision":"confirmed","reason":"'It needed a whole generation for the Times' pays off Delane's fixed ideas, and that setup is now gone, so the closing line lands unmotivated. The 'old scores' setup is partly covered by the ridicule clause, so I restore only the cortex clause.","evidence":[{"document":"013.source","paragraph":5,"quote":"the capture of Vicksburg had not yet penetrated Delane's thick cortex of fixed ideas."},{"document":"013.revision","paragraph":5,"quote":"It needed a whole generation for the Times to reach Milnes's standpoint."}]},{"id":"F3","decision":"rejected","reason":"The 1862 secrecy and the later revelation remain explicit. Paragraph 14 has 'burying in profound secrecy' and paragraph 15 dates the 1889 biography. Paragraph 9 keeps the loss of hope and the rising tone. The cut is a legitimate compression within the word budget.","evidence":[{"document":"013.revision","paragraph":14,"quote":"burying in profound secrecy his attempt to break up the Union in the autumn of 1862"},{"document":"013.revision","paragraph":9,"quote":"Little by little, Minister Adams lost hope. With loss of hope came the raising of tone"}]},{"id":"F4","decision":"confirmed","reason":"'They, too' follows 'the idea of his Government', so its subject is unclear. The repair names the subject; 'too' then contrasts with Seward's success, which the paragraph states earlier. The second point, 'Its practical value', is rejected: 'Its' can fairly attach to the battle and struggle just described, so no change is needed there.","evidence":[{"document":"013.revision","paragraph":13,"quote":"the idea of his Government. They, too, had shown power, patience and steadiness of purpose"},{"document":"013.source","paragraph":14,"quote":"but this was no discredit to Russell or Palmerston or Gladstone. They, too, had shown power"}]},{"id":"F5","decision":"confirmed","reason":"The source says no one else felt any suspicion. 'Doubted' can be read as everyone being certain, which reverses the irony behind Russell's naïve 'suspicious'. A minimal wording restoration fixes it.","evidence":[{"document":"013.source","paragraph":20,"quote":"when no one else in Europe or America felt any suspicion about it"},{"document":"013.revision","paragraph":18,"quote":"calling \"suspicious\" what no one else in Europe or America doubted"}]}],"replacements":[{"old":"at the moment of Milnes's embrace. He had never heard of young Adams","new":"at the moment of Milnes's embrace. Delane probably regarded it as a piece of Milnes's foolery. He had never heard of young Adams","reason":"Restores source sentence so the pronoun refers to Delane.","finding_ids":["F1"]},{"old":"letter from Manchester. It needed a whole generation","new":"letter from Manchester. The capture of Vicksburg had not yet penetrated Delane's thick cortex of fixed ideas. It needed a whole generation","reason":"Restores source setup for the 'whole generation' quip.","finding_ids":["F2"]},{"old":"They, too, had shown power","new":"Russell and Palmerston, too, had shown power","reason":"Clarifies the referent, matching the source's discussion of Russell and Palmerston.","finding_ids":["F4"]},{"old":"what no one else in Europe or America doubted","new":"what no one else in Europe or America felt any suspicion about","reason":"Restores source wording; avoids inverting the point.","finding_ids":["F5"]}],"remaining_concerns":["'Its practical value as education' in paragraph 13 remains slightly loose but readable."]}
